courseTitle: Physics 2: Fluids, Heat, Electricity, Light and Atoms
title: Power in Resistors
short: P = IV = I²R = V²/R are three forms of one idea.
trouble: Students conclude that a bigger resistor always uses more power, missing that in parallel the smaller one does.

blocks.html: A resistor turns electrical energy into thermal energy: that is how toasters, heaters and old-style light bulbs work. In Electric Power and Energy Use you met $P = IV$. Combined with $V = IR$ and what you know about resistance, it comes in three forms.

Each coulomb that crosses a resistor drops through a potential difference $V$, so it gives up $V$ joules. If $I$ coulombs cross each second, the resistor receives $IV$ joules per second: $P = IV$. Substituting Ohm's law: with $V = IR$, $P = I^2R$; with $I = V/R$, $P = V^2/R$. They are one idea; pick the form that uses what you know.

$$\role{power}{P} = \role{current}{I}\role{voltage}{V} = \role{current}{I}^2\role{resistance}{R} = \frac{\role{voltage}{V}^2}{\role{resistance}{R}}$$ Same current (series): the bigger resistor uses more power. Same voltage (parallel): the smaller resistor uses more power. Energy $=$ power $\times$ time; $1\,\text{kWh} = 3.6 \times 10^{6}\,\text{J}$.

blocks.name: ph-circuit
blocks.cap: Bulbs in series share one current, so the $8\,\Omega$ bulb ($I^2R$ larger) glows brighter.

blocks.name: ph-circuit
blocks.cap: Bulbs in parallel share one voltage, so now the $4\,\Omega$ bulb ($V^2/R$ larger) glows brighter. Try both in the Circuit Builder.

blocks.title: A lamp
blocks.q: A lamp on $120\,\text{V}$ draws $0.50\,\text{A}$. Find its power and its resistance.

blocks.title: Series: bigger wins
blocks.q: A $2\,\Omega$ and a $4\,\Omega$ resistor are in series on $12\,\text{V}$. Find each one's power.

blocks.title: Parallel: smaller wins
blocks.q: The same resistors are put in parallel on $12\,\text{V}$. Find each one's power.

blocks.html: Concluding that a bigger resistor always uses more power. That is true only when the current is the same (series). With the same voltage (parallel), the smaller resistor lets more current through and uses more power, which is why a $1500\,\text{W}$ heater has a smaller resistance than a $60\,\text{W}$ lamp on the same outlet. Check: first decide what is shared, $I$ or $V$, then use $I^2R$ or $V^2/R$.
